name: Chin tuck
instruction: Slide your head straight back, like making a double chin.
steps: Sit or stand tall, shoulders relaxed, eyes level.
Without tilting your head, slide your chin straight back. A double chin is fine.
Hold 2 to 3 seconds. You should feel a light stretch where the head meets the neck.
Let your head slide back to the start. That is one rep.
tip: Keep your eyes level the whole time. If you nod, it becomes a different exercise.

name: Doorway stretch
instruction: Forearms on the door frame, lean gently forward.
steps: Stand in an open doorway and raise your arms to shoulder height, elbows bent to about 90 degrees.
Rest your forearms on both sides of the frame, palms forward.
Step one foot forward and lean in slowly until you feel a stretch across the chest and the front of the shoulders.
Hold 30 seconds, breathing normally, then step back and relax.
tip: Stretch only as far as is comfortable, and don't arch your lower back. No doorway nearby? Use one hand on a wall corner, one side at a time.

name: Shoulder blade squeeze
instruction: Squeeze the shoulder blades back and down, then release.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your arms hanging; bending the elbows to about 90 degrees makes it easier.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and slightly down, as if holding a pen between them.
Hold 2 seconds.
Relax completely and repeat, 15 reps in all.
tip: Don't shrug your shoulders toward your ears or push your ribs forward. The movement is small and comes from the upper back.

name: Get up and walk
instruction: Get up and walk around, fill a glass, rest your eyes.
steps: Stand up and walk for 2 minutes. A lap around the office or a trip for water both count.
Let your arms swing and drop your shoulders.
On the way, look at something 6 m (20 ft) away for about 20 seconds to rest your eyes.
tip: Leave your phone on the desk. Your eyes need the break too.

name: Upper back extension
instruction: Hands behind your head, lean your upper back over the chair.
steps: Sit all the way back so the top of the chair back meets the middle of your back, below the shoulder blades.
Lace your fingers behind your head, elbows forward. The hands support the neck; they don't pull.
Lean back gently over the chair and lift your chest toward the ceiling.
Pause for one breath and sit back up, 10 reps in all.
tip: Bend from the upper back, not the lower back or neck. If the chair reclines or rolls, brace it first or skip this one.

name: Hip flexor stretch
instruction: Stand in a lunge, squeeze the glute and push the pelvis forward.
steps: Take a big step forward with one foot, both feet pointing ahead. Hold a desk if you like.
Bend the front knee slightly and keep the back leg long.
Squeeze the glute on the back-leg side, tuck your tailbone, and gently push your pelvis forward.
You should feel the stretch at the front of the back-leg hip. Hold 30 seconds, then switch legs.
tip: Keep your chest up. Arching your back to go deeper only moves the stretch somewhere useless.

name: Side neck stretch
instruction: Ear toward the shoulder, the other shoulder pressing down.
steps: Sit or stand tall, shoulders relaxed.
Slowly tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder, eyes still facing forward.
Keep the left shoulder down. For more stretch, reach your left hand toward the floor.
Hold 20 seconds, come back up slowly, and switch sides.
tip: Don't lift the shoulder to meet the ear, and don't pull your head with your hand.

name: Calf raise
instruction: Rise onto your toes, then lower slowly.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, one hand on a desk or wall for balance.
Push through the balls of your feet and rise as high as you can.
Pause 1 second at the top.
Take about 2 seconds to lower until your heels touch, 20 reps in all.
tip: Keep your weight over the big toes so the ankles don't roll outward.
